purpose: Section 20: compute the SAME pre-registered agreement statistics (08) over the SAME three independent adjudicators' fresh, isolated re-adjudication (17a/17b/17c) of the 22-case holdout (16) under REPLACEMENT_RUBRIC_V2 (15/_taxonomy-operational-rubric-v2-REPLACEMENT.json), to determine whether the one permitted rubric redesign restored reproducibility.

processIntegrityNote.issue: Adjudicator B self-reported that its private scratch temp file (outside the git repo, in this session's shared scratchpad directory) was overwritten mid-task by a complete result set belonging to Adjudicator A.
processIntegrityNote.investigation: Verified post-hoc, before trusting any result: (1) zero verbatim rationale-text matches between A and B across all 22 cases; (2) B's detailed-state disagreement rate with A (6 of 22, 27%) is NOT anomalously low relative to the other pairs - B in fact agrees MORE with C (18/22) than with A (16/22), the opposite of what copying from A would produce; (3) spot-checked case-by-case reasoning shows B applying a genuinely different, independently-derived interpretation of the rubric's INCOMPARABLE 'override evidence' language than A on 4 of the 4 conmed cases, disagreeing with A's conclusion in each - this is affirmative evidence of independent reasoning, not contamination.
processIntegrityNote.conclusion: No evidence any adjudicator's final output was influenced by another's work. The results below are used as reported.
processIntegrityNote.infrastructureRiskDisclosed: The Agent tool's per-session scratchpad directory is shared across all subagents dispatched in one session and is not adjudicator-isolated by default. This phase's dispatch instructions told each adjudicator to write ONLY to its own designated final output path in the repo (which worked correctly - no cross-writes occurred there), but did not enforce isolated TEMP/scratch paths, which is what collided here. Carried forward to 24-remaining-evaluator-risks.json as a required infrastructure fix for any future reuse of this methodology: give each blinded adjudicator a unique scratch subdirectory explicitly, not just a unique final-output path.

pairwiseDetailedAgreement_excludingUnres.note: No UNRESOLVED_CONSENSUS cases occurred in this holdout (unlike the original 65-case study's 5) - a clean 2-of-3 detailed majority was reached on every case. This metric is therefore identical to the all-cases metric above.

binary.interpretation: MANDATORY DISCLOSURE per 08's pre-registration: this near-zero (slightly negative) kappa does NOT mean binary agreement is poor - it is the well-known artifact of extreme category skew (all three raters chose NO_CREDIT on 21-22 of 22 cases; the marginal distribution is ~98% one category). When one category dominates this heavily, the chance-agreement baseline (P_e_bar) is itself close to 1, so even near-perfect observed agreement (P_bar=0.97) yields a chance-adjusted statistic near zero. Per the pre-registration, the RAW pairwise agreement (96.97%) is the actual pass/fail gate, not kappa - kappa is disclosed here exactly as required, not substituted as an alternate gate, and does not change the binary gate's PASS result below.

detailed.interpretation: Moderate-to-substantial agreement (Landis-Koch scale), meaningfully lower than the original study's detailed kappa (0.64) despite the rubric clarification - the chance-adjustment does not rescue this result either; it corroborates the raw rate's failure.

comparisonToOriginalStudy.direction: WORSE on the holdout, not better - the replacement rubric's two precision clarifications did not close the gap; if anything the holdout's heavier concentration of exactly the targeted mechanisms (chapeau/composite claims, sibling-adjacency) combined with a NEW confusable pair the original sample never surfaced (INCOMPARABLE vs DISCOVERED_ONLY, driven by CONMED's blank-literal-excerpt ground-truth authoring style) made detailed agreement harder, not easier.

newConfusionPatternDiscoveredOnHoldout.diagnosis: All 4 CONMED cases in the holdout (a-7.2-a/b/c/e) have a ground-truth unit whose groundTruthExcerpt field is literally empty with groundTruthExcerptResolution='UNRESOLVED_DESCRIPTION_ONLY' (CONMED's ground-truth was authored by paraphrased description only, not verbatim excerpt, for its enumerated basket sub-items). Adjudicator A treated this as satisfying INCOMPARABLE's necessary condition outright on all 4. Adjudicators B and C instead applied INCOMPARABLE's own sufficient-condition caveat ('AND no override evidence exists that would let a reviewer confidently resolve the ground-truth unit's own meaning') and found that an exact-quoting inventory candidate constituted such 'override evidence,' resolving the claim's meaning and excluding INCOMPARABLE - then evaluated the resolved claim as DISCOVERED_ONLY.
newConfusionPatternDiscoveredOnHoldout.implication: This is a THIRD distinct rubric-precision gap (in addition to the two the redesign already fixed), located in the INCOMPARABLE state's own 'override evidence' language, which 06/the REPLACEMENT rubric never precisely defined. It was not visible in the original 65-case sample because none of those ground-truth units used CONMED's blank-excerpt/description-only authoring convention as heavily. This is disclosed as evidence that a genuinely reproducible taxonomy for this corpus may require MORE than the one redesign this phase permits - see 24-remaining-evaluator-risks.json and 25-final-verdict.json.

conclusionPerSection20: The replacement rubric FAILED to restore detailed reproducibility on a fresh, never-before-seen holdout, and did so more severely than the original study, with a newly-surfaced confusable pair the redesign did not anticipate or address. Per Section 20's explicit instruction ('if the replacement ALSO fails reproducibility, STOP - do not design ontology V3 - return NEEDS_ARCHITECTURE_DECISION'), no second (V3) redesign is attempted in this phase. See 18-replacement-ontology-freeze.json and 25-final-verdict.json.
